transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-06-05 15:00 PT
- Duration: ~42 minutes
- Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Samira (Lynx CTO), Ben (Lynx ML Eng), Priya (Lynx PM)

Auto Summary (brief): Discussed quickstart flow for Redwood hosted API, free credits and steps to get first token; also surfaced security and latency constraints that might push them to Dedicated or Private in the medium term. Agreed to share quickstart, a small benchmark spreadsheet, and schedule a pilot dry-run.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone thanks for joining, this is Jordan from Redwood, i have Maya our solutions engineer with me, how's everyone doing?
[00:05] Samira: Good, thanks. Samira here, CTO at Lynx, and we've got Ben and Priya on, thanks for setting this up.
[00:12] Maya: Hey all, quick agenda — we'll walk through our PLG quickstart path, what time-to-first-token looks like, and then dig into any infra or compliance blockers you have.
[00:20] Priya: Sounds good. We're mainly trying to understand if we can start on your hosted API and later move to dedicated capacity or private deployment. Also want to know how much work it is to get a POC running.
[00:30] Jordan: Totally. The typical path for teams like you is self-serve sign-up, free credits, run the quickstart (we have SDK + curl examples) and you'll get a token in under 10 minutes, often less. If you need predictable latency or data isolation, Dedicated is the midterm option, and Private (VPC or on-prem) is for regulated data.
[00:48] Ben: Curious about the free credits — is that enough to run a pilot of like a few hundred thousand tokens? And also any rate limits?
[00:55] Jordan: Good question. We usually offer enough credits to run a small pilot, depends on the program but typically covers a few hundred thousand tokens. Rate limits are configurable; for self-serve there's a baseline and you can request increases. For Dedicated it's fully configurable in the contract.
[01:08] Samira: Our main worry is latency. We have a 200ms P50 target for short responses (<=256 tokens). Do you have published latency numbers?
[01:17] Maya: We do — we publish perf profiles per model. For hosted endpoints in our US West region with opt-quant models you can often be around ~60-120ms for small responses P50, but it depends on model and traffic. For guaranteed 200ms P50 at scale you'd typically look at Dedicated and some routing policies. Also worth noting we do automatic batching, prefix/KV cache — sorry, KV cash in the transcript — to reduce cost and improve throughput.
[01:40] Ben: When you say routing policies, do you mean auto-fallbacks to cheaper variants if capacity is constrained, or more like region failover?
[01:46] Maya: Both. You can set policies by latency, cost, or region — e.g., prefer a low-latency GPU pool, fallback to a smaller variant if overloaded. That gives resilience for production apps.
[01:56] Priya: For us security is a big piece — we need SOC 2, SSO (SAML), RBAC, audit logs, and KMS integration. How does Redwood handle that on hosted?
[02:06] Jordan: Hosted customers get SOC 2 and basic SSO integrations; audit logs and per-route observability are available. For KMS and a private control plane you can do Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) which plugs into customer-managed KMS. We'll share the security whitepaper link after this call.
[02:21] Samira: If we start hosted, is there a way to later export keys or migrate models/use the same API without code changes?
[02:27] Maya: Yes, part of our design is the same API across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private. You can pin model versions and rollover configuration so your client code doesn't need major changes. There are some infra migration steps but functionally the API surface is stable.
[02:41] Ben: Another practical question — what about embeddings and batching for our search use case? We expect to embed at scale and then use a nearest-neighbor index. Does hosted support that well?
[02:50] Jordan: Hosted supports embeddings and has rate-limited pipelines for high-volume workloads. If you want consistent throughput for high-volume embed ingestion, Dedicated pools or autoscaling bursts are common. We also offer intelligent batching suggestions via Redwood Optimize.
[03:05] Priya: Time-to-first-token — can you walk us through the exact steps? We want to give devs a checklist.
[03:12] Maya: Sure: sign up -> verify email -> create API key in Console -> install SDK or run curl -> call /v1/generate with a short prompt. We have templates for Node/Python. If you follow the quickstart guide and use the sample key we send, a dev can run the first request in 5–10 minutes. There's also streaming SDK examples.
[03:30] Jordan: We'll send sample snippets and a free credits token so you can run end-to-end. Expect some rate-limiting on the sample key but enough to do functional tests.
[03:37] Ben: One more infra note — we have some EU data residency needs for customer data. If we start on Hosted US, what's the path?
[03:44] Maya: We have regional endpoints — EU regions are available. For strict residency you might go Private with VPC and customer-managed networking. We'll capture your compliance details and propose options in the follow-up.
[03:55] Priya: What's the typical timeline if we want a Dedicated proof-of-concept?
[04:00] Jordan: Usually a week or two to stand up a dedicated pool for a pilot, depending on capacity and contract, but for early-stage pilots teams usually validate on Hosted first with free credits, then move to Dedicated once they see usage patterns.
[04:12] Samira: Cost — can you give a rough sense of cost for hosted vs dedicated? We want to compare unit economics to our in-house GPU costs and OpenAI pricing.
[04:20] Maya: Hosted is usage-based per-token, which is easiest to start with. Dedicated is a reserved capacity contract — more predictable for heavy workloads and often lower per-token cost. We can run a cost model based on your 1M token/month projection. We'll include that spreadsheet.
[04:33] Ben: Any gotchas on model compatibility — we currently run a trimmed LLaMA variant in-house; can you host custom models?
[04:40] Maya: We onboard models — open models are supported and we have a model catalog. For private/custom models there's a process for model onboarding; we'll coordinate with your infra team for artifacts and compatibility.
[04:51] Jordan: Also to foreshadow technical deep dives — if you're interested in perf tuning (quantization, kernel selection, sequence length distribution), Maya can run a focused session.
[04:59] Ben: Yes please, we'd want a deep dive if we get to pilot.
[05:03] Priya: Ok let's talk success criteria for the pilot — for us it would be: 1) integration in dev environment within 2 weeks, 2) under 200ms P50 on representative short prompts, 3) cost at or below X per 1k tokens (we'll fill exact number).
[05:19] Jordan: That sounds reasonable. We'll align on exact numbers offline and include as acceptance criteria.
[05:24] Samira: One small note — do you have RBAC scoped keys so certain teams only see logs for their projects?
[05:30] Maya: Yes, we have token scoping and role-based controls in Console. Audit logs and per-route cost breakdowns are supported. For very strict org setups we recommend Private where you control the control plane.
[05:41] Ben: About benchmarking — we can share a set of 20 representative prompts, some 50–100 tokens, some 1–2k tokens. Would you run them against hosted and provide a simple latency/cost matrix?
[05:51] Maya: Absolutely, share the prompt set and we'll do a small benchmark. We'll return a simple sheet with P50/P95 numbers and token cost estimates.
[05:59] Jordan: Quick housekeeping — we'll send: 1) quickstart guide + sample snippet + free credits link, 2) security whitepaper, 3) benchmark spreadsheet template, 4) scheduling options for the SE deep dive.
[06:12] Priya: Perfect. Any closing concerns from you, Samira/Ben?
[06:17] Samira: No major ones. Just want to make sure we protect customer data and minimize migration effort later.
[06:22] Ben: Same. Also want to validate memory/KV cache behavior for conversation state in the deep dive.
[06:28] Maya: Noted — we'll include KV cache notes and examples; occasionally the transcript spelled it KV cash in older docs, ignore that.
[06:36] Jordan: Great, we'll follow up with the artifacts and set up the pilot schedule. Thanks everyone.
[06:40] Priya: Thanks, bye.
[06:42] Samira: Bye.

End of transcript.

References mentioned:
- Redwood quickstart: https://console.redwood.ai/quickstart
- Security whitepaper (shared post-call): https://redwood.ai/security-whitepaper.pdf
- Benchmark spreadsheet (template): link to be shared by Maya

Recap / Agreed next steps (also in metadata): Jordan sends quickstart + credits; Maya shares benchmark template; team to schedule SE deep dive in 1 week; Ben to prepare prompts.
